extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians, students, and philosophers concerned with the foundations and rigor of calculus (fluxions/infinitesimals)
extracted.subtask_description: A philosophical and mathematical critique of the fluxionary (calculus) method, arguing standards for legitimate demonstration, the treatment of infinitesimals, and the logical/conceptual foundations of fluxions (velocities).

rubrics_metrics.name: No geometrical quantity can be exhausted by division
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘no Geometrical Quantity, can by any Division or Subdivision whatsoever be exhausted, or reduced to nothing.’
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantities should not be treated as capable of becoming literally nothing by subdivision; methods that implicitly assume quantities can be reduced to zero by successive division are illegitimate. Example/implication: one must not justify throwing away infinitesimal parts by treating them as literally zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs must proceed from principles to conclusions, not invert the order
rubrics_metrics.description: The inverted Way of demonstrating your Principles by your Conclusions ... is contrary to the Rules of Logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A valid mathematical demonstration must derive conclusions from established principles and premises; one must not infer the truth of foundational principles from their (possibly correct) consequences. Anti-pattern: asserting principles because their consequences appear true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors in premises produce proportional errors in conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: whatever Errors are admitted in the Premises, proportional Errors ought to be apprehended in Conclusion, be they finite or infinitesimal
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot dismiss small errors in premises as harmless: an inaccuracy in premise leads to a corresponding inaccuracy in conclusion. Consequently, rejecting small terms (infinitesimals) must be justified, not assumed safe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth obtained by canceling compensating errors is not scientific demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: I observe ... that the Conclusion comes out right, not because the rejected Square of dz. was infinitely Small; but because this Error was compensated by another contrary and equal Error ... though you arrive at the Truth not knowing how or by what Means. To call that Science is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If correct results arise only because multiple inconsistent errors cancel, that does not amount to proper demonstration. The method must show how the conclusion legitimately follows, not rely on fortuitous compensation of mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: You must not reject infinitesimals except by legitimate algebraic annihilation
rubrics_metrics.description: o cannot be thrown out as an Infinitesimal, or upon the Principle that Infinitesimals may be safely neglected, But only because it is destroyed by an equal Quantity with a negative Sign, whence 0–p0 is equal to nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglecting an increment (infinitesimal) is only legitimate when equal quantities are subtracted from both sides or canceled by equal opposite terms. Simply discarding a term as 'infinitesimal' without such algebraic justification is illegitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of subtracting equals: algebraic axiom must be respected
rubrics_metrics.description: If from Equals you subtract Equals, the Remainders will be equal. ... it is illegitimate to keep an Equation, by subtracting from one Side a Quantity when it is not to be destroyed, or when an equal Quantity is not subtracted from the other Side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operations that remove terms must follow algebraic axioms: you cannot remove a term from one side unless you remove a corresponding equal term (or show it's zero) from the other. This is a necessary condition for legitimate symbolic manipulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent or contradictory suppositions in geometric argument
rubrics_metrics.description: it is sophistical to suppose NO or RP, PS, and SK to be finite real Lines in order to form the Triangle RP S ... and afterwards to suppose there are no such Lines, nor consequently similar Triangles, and nevertheless to retain the Consequence of the First Supposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't assume geometric objects both exist and do not exist within the same chain of reasoning. A method that first requires finite lines (to get proportions) and later supposes they vanish (while keeping consequences) is logically inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: A line cannot be both tangent and secant; limits must be handled consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: the Subsecant will always be less than the Subtangent, and can never coincide with it; which Coincidence to suppose would be absurd ... the same Line at the same Time to cut and not to cut another given Line, which is a manifest Contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit procedures that pretend a secant becomes exactly the tangent while retaining proportions derived from secants are illicit. One must treat limiting positions and the objects used to derive relations consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluxions (velocities) cannot be conceived independently of space and time
rubrics_metrics.description: we have no Notion of Velocity prescinded from Time and Space ... the Notion of Velocities being only composed of the direct Proportion of the Spaces, and the reciprocal Proportion of the Times
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any account of fluxions that treats them as abstract magnitudes independent of space and time is defective. Velocities must be grounded in measurable notions (lengths and times); otherwise their ratios and proportions lack meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluxionary definitions must not rely on obscure or inconceivable steps
rubrics_metrics.description: if, in order to arrive at these finite Lines proportionate to the Fluxions, there be certain Steps made use of which are obscure and inconceivable, be those finite Lines themselves ever so clearly conceived, it must nevertheless be acknowledged that your proceeding is not clear nor your Method scientific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if final, finite substitutes for fluxions are clear, the method is defective if reaching them requires opaque or unintelligible reasoning. Methods should be transparent and leave principles and steps comprehensible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points and triangles: avoid forming geometric creatures at a point
rubrics_metrics.description: A Point therefore is considered as a Triangle, or a Triangle is supposed to be formed in a Point. Which to conceive seems quite impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on metaphorical or logically impossible constructions (like treating a point as if it has area/triangle) as parts of rigorous argument. Limit notions must be expressed without asserting geometrically impossible identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportions require measurable magnitudes; ratios of velocities demand measures
rubrics_metrics.description: To consider the Proportion or Ratio of Things implies that such Things have Magnitude: That such their Magnitudes may be measured, and their Relations to each other known ... there is no measure of Velocity except Time and Space
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot meaningfully state proportions of abstract velocities unless you provide measurable magnitudes (lengths and times) to ground those ratios. Demands clarity on what is being measured before forming proportional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: The analyst (mathematician) should be judged as a logician: examine premises and inference
rubrics_metrics.description: I consider the Geometrical Analyst as a Logician, i.e. so far forth as he Reasons and Argues, and his Mathematical Conclusions, not in themselves, but in their Premises; ... not as true or false, useful or insignificant, but as derived from such Principles, and by such Inferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mathematical work by the soundness and clarity of its premises and inferences, not only by the apparent truth of its conclusions. Explicitly check how each conclusion follows from premises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume infinitesimals vanish without destroying their consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not legitimate or logical to suppose o to vanish, i.e. to be nothing, unless we reject at the same Time with the Increment itself every Consequence of such Increment, i.e. whatsoever could not be obtained but by supposing such Increment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If one treats an increment as zero, one must also remove every derived term that depended on it; selectively discarding consequences is invalid. Practical implication: when omitting higher-order terms, ensure corresponding consequences are also omitted or canceled legitimately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naming signs is easy; forming clear ideas of fluxions without measures is not
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is easier than to assign Names, Signs, or Marks to these Fluxions ... But it will be found much more difficult, to omit the Signs and yet retain in our Minds the things, which we suppose to be signified by them ... to form a clear and distinct Idea of any Velocity at all, exclusive of and from all Length of Time and Space ... is impossible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbolic notation alone does not constitute understanding. One must supply conceptual/measurable content to symbols (fluxions) rather than rely on manipulative signs without clear ideas of what they denote.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid inconsistent algebraic suppositions (e.g., assuming unequal then equal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide now z^2 − x^2 by z − x and the Quotient will be z + x + ... supposing that z and x are equal, this same Quotient will be 3 * x which in that case is the Ordinate ... But herein is a direct Fallacy: for in the first place, it is supposed that the Abscissae z and x are unequal, without which no one step could have been made; and in the second place, it is supposed they are equal; which is a manifest Inconsistency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not perform derivations that require contrary suppositions (first that variables differ, later that they coincide) without carefully treating the limiting transition. Logical consistency of hypotheses throughout manipulation is required.
